races.name: Kenny Developments Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Bridge View Star
runners_data.note: 302 days off the track is a major concern; has finished no better than third in four hurdle starts on similar going, and the wide-margin hold-up style means it is unlikely to secure any sort of meaningful position in a 23-runner field.

runners_data.name: Deeter
runners_data.note: OR 120 is the highest-rated runner but carries a finish-fading flag and has pulled up in its most recent start; Simon Torrens rides but the pattern of weakening late is damaging in a race that will suit those who stay close to the pace.

runners_data.name: En Or
runners_data.note: Best similar-going record amongst the deeper-tracking types (1W3P from 15 runs on soft/good-to-soft); A J Martin yard returns 2/7 over 14 days and the step back to a maiden context could suit, though the horse will be tracking wide in a 23-runner field.

runners_data.name: Firebrand
runners_data.note: Consistent in placing terms — four placed efforts from five runs, all on good or good-to-soft ground — and Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim gives a weight advantage; the prominent style is the best natural fit for the race shape Wonderful Everyday creates.

runners_data.name: Its Time For A Run
runners_data.note: Won a Gowran maiden on good in the most recent start and Emmet Mullins sends it here in good order (1/7 over 14 days); true hold-up tendency means securing a forward berth in this field will be harder than the map suggests, marginally discounting its chance.

runners_data.name: Leva Eagle
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed with no public form or going data available; Norman Lee yard has only one runner over 14 days and the amateur jockey Mr E M Nugent takes the ride, adding further uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Minnatrix
runners_data.note: Five runs on good ground all with ordinary finishes (best a second on debut); the persistent fading flag in finish is a clear negative in a race where those who can sustain their effort through the third-last will hold an advantage.

runners_data.name: Morale Boost
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a form string that includes a win but also a pulled-up effort, and has not run for 121 days; the unknown-going tag and lightly raced label flag a horse whose current readiness is genuinely opaque.

runners_data.name: Mr Caulfield
runners_data.note: Placed second over 21f on good going and showed staying ability; Noel Kelly has a quiet 14-day record (0/14) and the horse ran just seven days ago, so freshness is a consideration, but the style could suit a race run at a steady tempo.

runners_data.name: Papanell
runners_data.note: Four runs all on good or soft ground without a win; true hold-up style means it will be towards the rear of a 23-runner field and is unlikely to get a clear passage, limiting its realistic chance however fit and well it arrives.

runners_data.name: Piper Street
runners_data.note: Only one run to reference (sixth at Leopardstown on good), giving very little to work with; the hold-up style in a large field and the single data point make this one of the least well-profiled horses in the race.

runners_data.name: Tribal Thunder
runners_data.note: J J Slevin is a strong booking for this unknown-going type with lightly raced status; four runs including a third suggest some ability but the form string is patchy and the going tag remains a flag.

runners_data.name: Blue Nude
runners_data.note: Has finished in the top half of the field just once in four hurdle runs; the fade-in-finish flag and being a genuine hold-up type means it will be sectioned towards the rear of a large field, making a winning challenge highly unlikely.

runners_data.name: You Lift Me Up
runners_data.note: Two hurdle runs, both finishing seventh or worse; the P J Rothwell yard sends it here 10 days after its last start alongside stablemate Blue Nude, but there is nothing in the form to suggest a winning chance at this level.

runners_data.name: Getaway Tobin
runners_data.note: Four runs on good ground, all finishing between fourth and fourteenth; the genuine hold-up profile and lack of any win or place at this trip are negatives in a race where front position matters — will trail the field again.

runners_data.name: Hometomayo
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a modest form profile including two pulled-up efforts; the fade-in-finish tendency and amateur jockey Alan King (7lb) make this a very difficult proposition in a 23-runner field where pace positioning is critical.

runners_data.name: Leva Deva
runners_data.note: Four runs on good/good-to-soft, all finishing ninth or worse; the persistent fade flag and a race style that sees it naturally at the back of a large field means the race is likely to be won before this horse enters contention.

runners_data.name: Middlethird Marvel
runners_data.note: Six runs on good ground, best finish a sixth, and carries the fade-in-finish flag; Darren Collins has only one runner in the 14-day window and despite the prominent-horse label this runner has never demonstrated the ability to sustain a challenge.

runners_data.name: Rene's Gold
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan returns 1/18 over 14 days (modest) and the horse has finished eighth and ninth in its two public starts on good ground; the fade flag and lack of placed effort on similar going undermine its prospects.

runners_data.name: Wonderful Everyday
runners_data.note: W P Mullins and Paul Townend dominate proceedings as the sole confirmed front-runner; form figures of 726-55 are unspectacular but Mullins knows how to place and Townend will control the race from the front on yielding Galway ground.

runners_data.name: Minella Maverick
runners_data.note: No public form available and no jockey declared; John Patrick Ryan has 2/11 over 14 days which is respectable, but complete absence of form data makes meaningful assessment impossible.

runners_data.name: Stary Notions
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with no public form, no jockey declared and P M Lynch returning 0/0 over 14 days; total unknown on all fronts.

runners_data.name: Misty Valentine
runners_data.note: Three-run form string with a pulled-up, a fifteenth and a fell/unseated — no completed-race evidence of ability on similar going; the fade flag and an OR of 120 without any visible justification make this one to note only for market moves.

races.paceDynamic: Wonderful Everyday (Paul Townend/W P Mullins) is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 23-runner field and will set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without any meaningful pressure to quicken the pace artificially. The yielding ground at Galway further encourages a steady early tempo, which typically stretches out at the third-last and benefits those who travel economically through the race. Firebrand is the key prominent challenger, likely to sit just behind Wonderful Everyday and race in a clearly advantageous position, while Its Time For A Run, Middlethird Marvel, Leva Deva, and Papanell are all flagged as genuine hold-up or prominent types who will struggle to find their natural berth in such a large, congested field and may end up racing wide or deeper than ideal. With a single pace-setter dictating a controlled gallop on yielding ground over 2m½f, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit close to the tempo without expending energy, as the steady pace will not generate the late kick needed for true hold-up horses — those distributed to the rear face a legitimate positional disadvantage in a 23-runner maiden where gaps may not materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wonderful Everyday Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Wonderful Everyday is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a measured tempo throughout, dictating from the front.
scenarios.body: Paul Townend's mount rolls along on a comfortable lead on yielding Galway ground and, untouched by rivals, simply does not find a strong finisher in time; the prominent horses who tuck in behind exhaust less energy and are best-placed to mount any challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace set by Wonderful Everyday allows a prominent racer to sit just off the leader, travel well and collar them from the third-last.
scenarios.body: Firebrand, with a pattern of consistent placed efforts and strong form on similar going, is ideally suited to sit a length or two off the pace and produce a sustained run from the second-last where the yielding ground tests stamina; Its Time For A Run, a winner at Gowran on good going, is another who could slot into second or third and arrive with a challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is deceptively hot enough to string the field out and gaps open up from the third-last for a horse arriving from off the pace.
scenarios.body: En Or has the best similar-going form amongst the deeper-lying types (1W3P on soft/good-to-soft) and is trained by A J Martin to peak for this kind of test; the yielding ground and long Galway straight give latecomers a window, though the large field and compressed pace make this outcome genuinely difficult.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unknown Type Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly raced, unexposed runners (Leva Eagle, Tribal Thunder, Minella Maverick or Stary Notions) turns out to have significant untapped ability.
scenarios.body: A maiden hurdle of this size at a festival meeting historically delivers the occasional big-priced unexposed type who outclasses the exposed runners on debut form; Tribal Thunder (J J Slevin) and Leva Eagle are the most intriguing unknown quantities on jockey and trainer connections alone.

watchPoints.text: Wonderful Everyday is the only true front-runner in 23 and Paul Townend will control the race from the front — watch whether any rival is bold enough to challenge for the lead early, as that is the single factor most likely to change the outcome.

Firebrand (Alan O'Sullivan, 5lb claim) is the prominent horse best-suited to the pace shape and has four placed efforts; watch for it to be ridden to sit second or third from the start as the race's most natural challenger to the pace-setter.

Its Time For A Run (Emmet Mullins, Donagh Meyler) is a winner on good ground and is sent here fit from a run 55 days ago — watch to see if Meyler pushes forward early to secure a better position than the hold-up tag suggests, as a prominent ride would transform its chance.

The large field of 23 on yielding Galway ground will compress in the early stages — watch for trouble in running between the third and second-last where the pace is likely to quicken, particularly for hold-up horses stuck wide or on the inside rail without a clear run.

Tribal Thunder (J J Slevin) and Leva Eagle are the two lightly raced unknowns with the strongest jockey/trainer profiles — watch the market move in the final hour as any significant support would signal stable confidence in unexposed ability.

races.name: Anglo Printers Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Beckistine
runners_data.note: Hold-up type out of a 230-day absence, and while similar-going form reads 6/10 it includes a soft-ground placing; the long layoff and modest recent form string (4996P-) make it hard to see her picking off 22 rivals off a staying trip.|

runners_data.name: Mart Lane
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up horse lightly campaigned on soft ground (0W1P in similar going) who shaped with a little promise when fourth last time; the amateur rider (Mr Finian Maguire) and a 42-day break are minor queries in a competitive open handicap.|

runners_data.name: Palace Boy
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran running in a hood, whose best similar-going run was a win but who has been placed only twice in 14 comparable starts; needs to rediscover something from a 25-day freshener as his recent form includes a fifth on good ground.|

runners_data.name: Inthenickoftime
runners_data.note: Prominent-style six-year-old with an excellent 2W8P record in similar going across 15 runs — he travels close to the pace and his trainer Bolger sends him here in good order fresh from a placing 35 days ago; his natural position just off the pace is perfectly suited to what this race shape will create.|

runners_data.name: Crowsatedappletart
runners_data.note: Front-to-prominent operator wearing a hood and tongue-tie who has won four times on similar going (4W9P in 15 starts) and lands a first-time claiming rider reduction (5lb); his course-form record and willingness to race prominently make him one of the most dangerous hold-up/prominent horses in the field.|

runners_data.name: Paul Collins
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse on a tongue-tie who stayed on for third over 3m at Bellewstown 17 days ago; the step back in trip to 2m½f is a slight query, but his work-rate and the fact he handles good ground well are positives in a race where he can hunt closer than usual.|

runners_data.name: I'm All In
runners_data.note: Four-year-old Gordon Elliott runner who has shown a pattern of fading in the finish (tagged accordingly) across his last five runs, including two falls; the prominent style and lack of a clear stamina profile at this trip on yielding ground are concerns.|

runners_data.name: Jay Jay Zee
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 144 days off, with four solid similar-going efforts (1W3P in 8 runs) but a fall in his most recent start; the amateur jockey and the fitness question mark after that lengthy absence offset his genuine staying credentials.|

runners_data.name: Codger's Rock
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type with a 2/16f good-ground placing as his best in seven similar-going runs, but has not managed to win; at OR 98 he is well-handicapped on upward form and runs fresh off 12 days, though the big field is a concern for a horse who needs a clear run.|

runners_data.name: Roc My Haarth
runners_data.note: Returns from 158 days off following a winning run on soft (1/23f/SOF), and that course-distance win on comparable going is the key form line; the absence is a risk but Ray Hackett has him back for a reason and his stamina profile suits a strong-staying test.|

runners_data.name: Synchronize
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse — his best run came when second from the rear at 13f on good ground — placed into midfield on the map because the field contains too many rear-of-field types; his STYLE_FIT of 0.91 reflects that he is unlikely to get the race run to suit him, and a steady Dontcavein gallop will not manufacture the gaps he needs.|

runners_data.name: Dontcavein
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and the pivotal horse in the race shape; returns from 209 days off, wears a tongue-tie, and while his similar-going record reads 0W0P in one comparable effort, he needs only to bowl along uncontested — the critical question is whether the long absence has left him short enough to sustain the pace over 2m½f.|

runners_data.name: Euro Maker
runners_data.note: Won over this sort of trip on good ground (1/16f/GOO) and is a true closer; because the rear is congested he has been mapped to midfield, but his STYLE_FIT of 0.92 captures the reality that a slow front-runner's gallop will not generate the pace deficit he exploits — the fade pattern is also a flag.|

runners_data.name: Kome Dans Un Reve
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has yet to win in seven similar-going runs and whose form string (6/16f/GOO, 10/17f/GOO) confirms a horse that finishes mid-pack; held up by nature but shuffled into midfield here, the STYLE_FIT discount and fade-in-finish tag make him a difficult proposition.|

runners_data.name: Brother Hollie
runners_data.note: Four-year-old wearing a tongue-tie whose best effort is a third on good ground over 18f; in truth a hold-up horse, but the map places him in midfield given rear congestion — the modest form, young age, and STYLE_FIT of 0.93 all point to a horse who will need things to fall perfectly.|

runners_data.name: Colin's Friend
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead-trained five-year-old back from 216 days — the longest layoff in the field alongside Dontcavein — with a 0W0P record in three similar-going starts; the yard is in excellent form (T14: 5/25) but the absence and the redistribution out of his natural hold-up role are significant headwinds.|

runners_data.name: Hillstar Blues
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a fade-in-finish flag who has managed just 1W1P across 13 similar-going efforts; back from 24 days and carrying a 7lb allowance claim, but a horse who struggles to see out trips and is racing out of her natural hold-up position is hard to anchor at the top of any shortlist.|

runners_data.name: Arctic Piper
runners_data.note: Returns from 25 days; has fallen in three of his last five and his form reads P8P-F9 — the safety record over hurdles is a concern in a 23-runner field; one placing in 15 similar-going runs (0W1P) makes a winning effort hard to project.|

runners_data.name: I Feel Fine
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has finished fourth on good ground and sixth on yielding; the fade-in-finish flag and STYLE_FIT of 0.92 combine with a 53-day absence and no win in nine similar-going runs to make him a clear saver rather than a primary selection.|

runners_data.name: Million Dollar Man
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell sends out a five-year-old with a P-600 recent record and just three similar-going runs, all poor; the fade-in-finish flag, STYLE_FIT of 0.90, and OR 89 at the bottom of the weights make him statistically one of the weakest profiles in the race.|

runners_data.name: Speakasyoufind
runners_data.note: Has no jockey declared against her name, which is a red flag in itself; the fade flag and STYLE_FIT of 0.91 aside, her two best efforts (2/20f/GOO and 6/20f/GOO) came at longer distances, and 2m½f may be sharp for a horse who typically needs a real test of stamina.|

runners_data.name: Black Bamboo
runners_data.note: Highest-rated horse in the field at OR 114 but carrying 174lbs and no jockey listed; recent form reads 4009-0 across 15 similar-going starts (0W3P) and the weight burden at nine years old on yielding ground makes this a very difficult horse to support.|

runners_data.name: Cinnabar Moth
runners_data.note: Five-year-old at the bottom of the weights (OR 80, 140lbs) with consistent form — four times placed in his last five starts (4/16f/GOO, 9/16f/GOO, 5/16f/GOO, 5/16f/GOO) but winless; a true hold-up horse mapped into midfield due to rear congestion, and his STYLE_FIT of 0.91 reflects the positional compromise.|

races.paceDynamic: Dontcavein is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 23-horse field and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival to push him along — he will stride into a comfortable lead from flag to finish on yielding Galway ground, dictating a tempo entirely of his own choosing. Behind him, Inthenickoftime, Crowsatedappletart, I'm All In, and Roc My Haarth are the natural prominent types who will press forward into the first few positions, creating a clustered second rank but not a genuine pace duel. The remainder of the field — Synchronize, Euro Maker, Brother Hollie, Colin's Friend, and others — are true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because this race simply cannot accommodate all of them at the rear; their natural finishing kicks will be compromised by the sheer volume of traffic and the likelihood that they end up racing in a position that doesn't suit. With one front-runner setting a sustainable, controlled gallop on a right-handed track that rewards those who travel through the race, this shape most strongly favours prominent racers who can sit in Dontcavein's slipstream, save ground, and deliver a clean challenge at the second-last — hold-up horses needing a strong pace to be set up for them will find the race has not been run to suit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dontcavein Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Dontcavein is allowed to bowl along in front at his own pace and the prominent horses behind him cannot close the gap turning for home.
scenarios.body: Dontcavein dictates a comfortable rhythm from the front, conserving energy through the early stages and using his jumping to maintain the advantage; prominent horses close from second and third but the soft, controlled pace means the winner has plenty left entering the final flight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pouncers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners tracking Dontcavein travel strongly and overhaul him from the second-last hurdle on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Inthenickoftime or Crowsatedappletart, sitting just off the pace throughout, capitalise on their superior handicap form and better finishing speed once the final jump is cleared; the steady gallop means their stamina reserves are fully intact at the business end.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Thread Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely slow and a late rush from midfield horses finds gaps in the straight as the front rank ties up.
scenarios.body: Hold-up types like Synchronize or Euro Maker, both genuine closers redistributed into midfield, need a strong enough pace to have been set early — at this realistic tempo they must rely on tiring front-runners and a clean passage through 23 runners, both of which are uncertain.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos Scrambles Result
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes interference or a pile-up at a flight and reshuffles the order mid-race, opening the door for a horse that had been hidden in the pack.
scenarios.body: A 23-runner hurdle on yielding ground with multiple horses racing out of their natural positions creates a meaningful risk of a bunched midfield incident; Paul Collins or Crowsatedappletart, both with positional flexibility, could benefit from gaps created by fallers or checking horses.

watchPoints.text: Crowsatedappletart's claiming rider (5lb, Michael Kenneally) and superior similar-going record (4W9P) make him the most dangerous prominent challenger — watch whether he gets a clean split two out.|
Dontcavein's fitness after 209 days off is the race-deciding variable — if he ties up before the last flight the race is thrown open; watch his jumping

races.name: Deacy Gilligan Hurdle

runners_data.name: Thecompanysergeant
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Cromwell with excellent similar-going credentials (15/15 yielding-type runs logged); 1W5P on similar ground underlines stamina and consistency, and at OR 133 he may be competitive if Blood Destiny is caught out by the trip; blinkers on.

runners_data.name: Blood Destiny
runners_data.note: Mullins/Townend combination with the race's dominant front-runner; OR 141, course form, and 11/15 on similar going — the tactical question is whether a solo lead on yielding 2m5½f suits or exposes him, but he has the class to dictate his own fractions.

runners_data.name: Buddy One
runners_data.note: OR 142 top-weight with mixed recent form (6P40-8) for a trainer whose 14-day strike rate is quiet (0/3); headgear noted, similar-going record is decent (12/15), but the distance of 2m6f+ and erratic recent returns make him a risk at the weight.

runners_data.name: French Dynamite
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 11-year-old returning after 279 days off; French Dynamite's form is strong on similar going (14/15, 2W6P) and he clearly handles long trips, but the near nine-month absence is a serious concern, even if McNamara has placed him carefully before.

runners_data.name: Grann's Boy
runners_data.note: Six-year-old prominent racer with four wins on similar ground (13/15, 4W5P); Flanagan takes the ride and Grann's Boy's Galway/right-handed form is a positive, though his last two runs — 6th and 10th on good — hint he prefers some cut, which he gets here.

runners_data.name: Milan Forth
runners_data.note: In reality a prominent-racing type who races near the pace, but squeezed out of that slot by the volume of front-runners in this field; OR 120, strong similar-going profile (11/13, 3W5P) over 2m, but the style-fit compromise and a step up in class are real headwinds.

runners_data.name: Samui
runners_data.note: Elliott's OR 131 runner carries a genuine hold-up profile and a flawless similar-going record (15/15, 2W9P), yet is mapped to midfield by redistribution — his chance is real but tactically compromised; only 10 days since last run is worth noting with a 7lb claimer aboard.

runners_data.name: Paul's Dream
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins earlier in the season on similar going (14/15, 4W9P) make his recent form eye-catching; apprentice O'Sullivan (5) rides, which is a significant rider concession in a competitive Galway hurdle, and the step back up to OR-class rivals is steep.

races.paceDynamic: Blood Destiny (Paul Townend, Mullins) is the confirmed front-runner and will stride straight into the lead from the off, with no natural rival to challenge for that position — this is effectively uncontested pace-setting over 2m5½f on yielding ground at Galway. French Dynamite and Grann's Boy are genuine prominent types who will track up into second and third early, creating a strung-out but measured tempo behind Blood Destiny rather than a pressured, scorching gallop. The field holds more prominent and front-running types than the map can accommodate in their natural positions — Milan Forth and Samui are true hold-up/prominent horses pushed into artificial midfield slots, meaning their redistribution discounts their ability to run their ideal race. This race shape — a single dominant pace-setter dictating a controlled but honest gallop on yielding going over an extended trip — strongly favours hold-up horses with stamina and tactical speed to pounce off a genuine pace, and patient prominent types who can settle within striking range without burning energy early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Blood Destiny Dictates Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Blood Destiny is allowed to stride clear uncontested and Townend manages the fractions to preserve a finishing effort.
scenarios.body: Blood Destiny has a clean lead on yielding Galway ground, controls every tempo decision, and the field simply cannot reel him in when he quickens from the second-last; Townend's class advantage over this field is significant and the OR 141 rating reflects genuine quality.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Blood Destiny's enforced solo lead on yielding ground drains enough fuel that a staying closer can overhaul him on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Thecompanysergeant, with strong similar-going form and a consistent record around 2m-plus on good-to-soft variants, is ideally positioned to be produced with a late run off a genuine pace; Buddy One's headgear and stamina profile could also see him stay on at the death if the pace proves just honest enough to stop Blood Destiny.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Type Runs On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly honest on the yielding ground and the lead pair's energy is spent, allowing a well-placed prominent chaser to inherit the spoils.
scenarios.body: Grann's Boy, with four wins from similar-ground profiles and a proven Galway record, is ideally suited to track the pace from the front rank and pick off a tiring leader; French Dynamite's course-form and class at this trip make him a live each-way contender if he gets a clean jumping round after his lengthy absence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race and horses shuffled out of their natural positions manage to work their way into contention.
scenarios.body: Paul's Dream has shown back-to-back wins over similar trips and going and could benefit if prominent horses overcook it, though his apprentice rider faces a significant task in this company; Samui's strong similar-going record is a genuine flag but, placed in an artificial midfield berth rather than his natural hold-up position, his chance is structurally compromised here.

watchPoints.text: Blood Destiny (Townend/Mullins) goes to post as an uncontested solo leader — watch whether Townend elects to coast or truly exploit the gap, as a slow early tempo could bring the prominent runners dangerously close by the home turn.

French Dynamite returns after 279 days off and, while his going/trip profile is strong, watch his jumping sharpness in the first mile — any errors on the hurdles could cost him the prominent pitch he needs.

Milan Forth and Samui are both racing outside their natural positions due to field redistribution — watch whether either can work forward/back to their preferred spot early, as failure to do so significantly undermines their winning chances.

Grann's Boy showed his best form on softer variants and gets that here; watch how quickly Flanagan sends him up to cover the pace from early, as his chance is heavily dependent on getting the right position behind Blood Destiny.

races.name: WTW Willis Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners_data.name: Clone Cross
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner mapping at OR 97 who is tactically suited to dominating from the front; Kevin Healy's 7lb claim is a bonus, has 0 wins from 4 places on similar ground, and the STYLE_FIT flag notes she is racing out of natural role — her best chance is dictating from the front, which this race allows.

runners_data.name: Deise Crystal
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse with Phillip Enright aboard; 2m6½f trip looks ideal given her placed run at 2m5f, and her six qualifying runs on good-to-soft suggest she handles this going fine — she needs a strongly-run race to exploit her late style.

runners_data.name: Joshua Chamberlain
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win at 2m1f on soft and consistent placed form at Galway distances; trainer Gerard Keane in quiet form (0/10 in 14 days) but the horse's own credentials over this trip and going mark him as a key player tracking the pace.

runners_data.name: Fair Damsel
runners_data.note: Lightly-weighted hold-up mare at OR 93 with recent form figures of 60-5D0 suggesting she is out of form; Danny Gilligan rides and her best placed efforts came at shorter, so the step to 2m6½f is a question.

runners_data.name: John Storey
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing tongue-tie, with a placed run at 2m5f on soft and a win at 2m1f on heavy — the stamina and going combination suits in theory, but his recent sequence of pulled-ups is a significant concern before placing confidence in him.

runners_data.name: Ladiam
runners_data.note: Tongue-tied prominent racer whose consistent placed form at Galway distances (3rd at 2m, 4th at 2m2f) on good ground gives him a reliable profile; Conor Smithers claiming 7lbs is an advantage and he should travel comfortably behind Clone Cross.

runners_data.name: The Little Yank
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse in cheekpieces at age 11 who has placed figures of 3,3 at 2m5f on good — goes well fresh and gets a 19-day return — but his sim-going record of 0 wins from 3 places flags limited upside at this level.

runners_data.name: Barryroe Madam
runners_data.note: Hood-wearing hold-up mare whose recent form (0-0040) and heavy weight do not inspire confidence; trainer Terence O'Brien had one runner in the last 14 days and her best placed effort (4th at 3m) came at a longer trip than this.

runners_data.name: Hickeys Hill

races.paceDynamic: Clone Cross is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 23-runner field and faces no meaningful pace duel, meaning she can control from the front at a rhythm entirely of her choosing over 2m6½f on yielding ground. With Hickeys Hill and Ladiam likely to push up prominently behind her, the pace will be honest but not frantic — a sustainable gallop that rewards those who can travel efficiently in the first half of the race and sustain their effort up the Galway hill. This shape is classic territory for the prominent-to-midfield racer who can sit just off the controlled pace, avoid traffic, and hit the front at the second-last; true hold-up horses face a structural problem given the field size and the bunching that a controlled pace creates in a 23-runner handicap. The race shape decisively favours prominent racers and positive-jumping types who can track Clone Cross without burning petrol, rather than those who need a fast pace to soften the field ahead of them. Note that the field contains significantly more true hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Princess Felicia, Coup d'Essay, Tedworth, Ranger Billy, Katie's Casper, Moonshine Girl and others are genuine closers who will be forced into unfamiliar midfield slots, compressing the pack and increasing the advantage for horses who can cleanly access the rail and travel near the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Clone Cross Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Clone Cross sets a sustainable tempo unchallenged and the race develops into a test of relentless galloping stamina on the Galway hill.
scenarios.body: Clone Cross dictates a strong but measured pace and Joshua Chamberlain or Ladiam, tracking just off her shoulder, have the clearest run to the front at the business end; the compressed midfield suits those who can jump fluently and avoid traffic at the cross-hurdles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Finishers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Clone Cross slows the race to a crawl early, creating a falsely-run contest that allows the compressed midfield pack to mass-deliver closers in the straight.
scenarios.body: A slow early gallop paradoxically helps those redistributed hold-up types who can produce a sharp turn of foot from midfield, though they must overcome the disadvantage of an unfamiliar position and traffic through a tightly-bunched field; Princess Felicia and Kilkee Bay have the class records to capitalise if gaps appear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Grinds Out Front
scenarios.trigger: If the yielding ground rides heavier than stated and the race becomes a thorough examination of stamina from an honest gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Horses with proven form at this trip or beyond on soft ground come into their own as the field strings out from the second-last; Joshua Chamberlain's win on soft and John Storey's placed efforts on similar ground give them the profile, and the long Galway run-in punishes those without genuine staying reserves.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scenario, Big Field Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If the large field generates early scrimmaging, multiple fallers or significant interference disrupts the tactical order mid-race.
scenarios.body: With 23 runners over hurdles on yielding ground, a pile-up or cascade of faller-related incidents can scramble the race entirely, handing opportunity to horses with wide draws or early speed who avoid trouble; those nearest the pace and with clean air — Clone Cross, Hickeys Hill — benefit most from surviving chaos intact.

watchPoints.text: Clone Cross controls the pace and any significant market move for Joshua Chamberlain in the 10 minutes before off would confirm prominent-racer confidence, as he is the horse best placed to track and challenge on the home turn.

The 23-runner field creates severe traffic risk at the early hurdles — watch for any scrimmaging behind Clone Cross that disrupts the holds-up types squeezed into midfield, particularly around Katie's Casper, Moonshine Girl and Phildante who are all naturals for the rear.

Princess Felicia carries the fades-in-finish flag despite strong recent form — if she is held up in midfield rather than her natural rearward position and the pace is not strong enough to soften those ahead, her fade tendency could cost her in the final 2f.

runners_data.name: Hey Babbs

runners_data.name: Grace Faraday
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature whose cheekpiece headgear and course form are positives, but the 108-day absence and the redistribution away from her true rear position mean she faces a stiffer positional challenge than her style ideally suits.

runners_data.name: The Vegas Raider
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old whose TV headgear and recent fall/unseated record (U, F in form) are significant negatives; mapped forward of natural position and the 14-day turnaround adds doubt rather than confidence.

runners_data.name: Poetic Focus
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's tongue-tied hold-up type has only one place from 13 sim-going runs — good recent trainer stats (7/23 over 14 days) are mildly interesting but the horse's form profile is weak and it races ahead of its natural rear-of-field station here.

runners_data.name: Agent Tequila
runners_data.note: A 174-day layoff is a major negative for this eight-year-old whose fade flag and tongue-tie compound concerns — true rear-of-field runner who would need everything to fall perfectly, which it rarely does after such a break.

runners_data.name: Itaintmebabe
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's seven-year-old has won on soft and placed on similar ground, but the tongue-free record on good going shows limited wins — the natural hold-up style is compressed by the large field.

runners_data.name: Three By Two

runners_data.name: Coppola
runners_data.note: Two placed efforts at 24f on good ground for Gordon Elliott, but consecutive P and U finishes and a fade flag are serious red flags — a hold-up horse whose redistribution forward adds further complication to an already poor recent record.

runners_data.name: Love Like This
runners_data.note: A busy seven-day turnaround for this eight-year-old; consistent place-hitting at 4th and 3rd in recent starts but no win in 15 sim-going starts — the activity and adaptability could help in chaos more than in a structured race.

runners_data.name: Tantrum Boy

runners_data.name: Vangaway
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a fade flag, only six outings on record, and a poor sim-going return (0W, 0P in 4 runs) — cheekpieces previously worn and the redistribution only adds to the concerns about finding a natural rhythm.

runners_data.name: Gortmore Lady
runners_data.note: Ciaran Murphy's six-year-old mare who has placed four times in 15 similar-going starts and finished third twice at shorter trips — the cheekpieces help her switch off and the consistent placing record makes her a live outsider in a messy finish.

runners_data.name: Tawny Lea

runners_data.name: Il Silenzio

runners_data.name: Phoenix Cowboy
runners_data.note: Returning after 430 days — an enormous layoff for a nine-year-old who was last placed at 17f; the trip, the absence and the absence of a jockey named all point to this being a fitness run rather than a winning opportunity.

runners_data.name: Simpletwistoffaith
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old with no wins or places in 15 sim-going starts and a recent form string of P/P69 — the layoff of 17 days is fine but the underlying form offers no reason to expect a turnaround in a competitive 23-runner handicap.

races.paceDynamic: Three By Two is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 23-runner field, and with no genuine challenger for the lead identified, J J Slevin can control fractions from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop over 2m6½f on yielding ground at Galway. The sheer volume of hold-up types — Grace Faraday, The Vegas Raider, Poetic Focus, Agent Tequila, Itaintmebabe, Il Silenzio and several others — means the field is stacked with horses that want to come from off the pace, yet only Three By Two and Max Time are mapped anywhere near the front, giving the leader a largely uncontested platform. This shape — one unhurried pace-setter, a compressed midfield chasing late, and a staying trip on soft-ish ground — classically rewards horses who can travel prominently or make smooth headway from a midfield berth, rather than true hold-up horses forced to make up excessive ground in one hit. The field holds materially more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; of those most likely to secure a forward position ahead of their natural style, Three By Two is alone confirmed, with Max Time the only other horse capable of pressing from the front, meaning the prominent-to-midfield profile that can track the leader holds the clearest positional advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Three By Two is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a moderate gallop that the chasing pack cannot quicken past.
scenarios.body: Three By Two rolls along at a comfortable pace over the staying trip, conserving enough energy to fight off challengers at the last, with Slevin able to control the race entirely from the front; horses who can travel prominently without burning energy — Strong Contender, Midleton Rare — are best placed to pounce if the leader weakens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Three By Two sets a genuine gallop and a prominent-to-midfield tracker times a run perfectly from second or third.
scenarios.body: The pace is genuine enough to string out the large field on the run to the last, and a horse travelling smoothly just behind the leader inherits the race as Three By Two ties up; Strong Contender's recent course-and-distance wins and Il Silenzio's sharp form profile both suit this shape well.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Three By Two goes too fast early on yielding ground and the field concertinas approaching the final two hurdles.
scenarios.body: A fast-run race collapses Three By Two's advantage and opens a window for hold-up horses making sweeping late runs, though the sheer number of genuine closers means traffic problems are highly likely in a 23-runner field; Journey So Far and L'As de Watt, the highest-rated hold-up types with going form, are best positioned to benefit if gaps open.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scramble Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes interference, bunching or fallers that disrupt the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: With 23 runners over 2m6½f on yielding ground, congestion in the final mile is a genuine risk that hands an advantage to horses tractable enough to switch and find room; Gortmore Lady's consistent place-hitting and Love Like This's recent activity suit the cut-and-thrust of a messy finish better than fragile hold-up types.

watchPoints.text: Three By Two is uncontested up front but returns after 215 days — watch for signs of the layoff telling on the final circuit, which would trigger an instant collapse in the pace shape.

With 23 runners on yielding ground at Galway's tight track, the risk of pile-ups, fallers or serious interference in the final mile is elevated — The Vegas Raider's recent fall and unseated record (U, F) makes him a specific traffic hazard to track runners behind him.

Strong Contender has two recent course-and-distance wins but is partnered by a 7lb claimer in Conor Smithers — watch whether that weight-saving translates to a positional advantage or whether the inexperience costs in a tight finish.

Il Silenzio has the strongest form profile of the genuine hold-up types but has no jockey named in the data — confirm the booking before the race as a late jockey change could alter confidence materially.

Max Time maps as a second prominent runner alongside Three By Two but his form (PP04P6) and fade flag suggest he will drift back quickly, effectively leaving Three By Two alone in front from an early stage and making the race even more one-dimensional than it already appears.

runners_data.name: Mongibello

races.paceDynamic: Mongibello is the confirmed front-runner here and, returning from a 501-day absence, will be allowed to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop on yielding ground at Galway — a track that already tests stamina through its undulations without needing a scorched-earth pace. With no natural rival willing to challenge him for the lead, he should dictate every yard of this 2m2f beginners' chase and set a rhythm that suits a relaxed, accurate jumper rather than a strong finisher. The field carries more genuine prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Polepatrick, Ndaawi, and Captain Ryan Matt are all natural front-to-prominent runners who will be squeezed back from their preferred positions and must race out of role. That compression of pace-pressing types into the midfield group creates a race likely to be won either by Mongibello controlling from the front or by a genuine hold-up horse who can travel easily off the modest tempo and produce a clean, measured finish — this race shape most clearly favours a prominent-to-front profile or an authentic hold-up horse with strong form on similar ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mongibello Controls Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Mongibello travels fluently on his comeback and jumps cleanly enough to maintain his lead into the straight.
scenarios.body: Coming back after 501 days, Mongibello's class (OR 128, highest in the field) and natural front-running style give him a significant edge if fitness holds, and his soft/good-to-soft form record of 8/9 sim-going runs with 3 wins is particularly relevant on yielding Galway ground. A steadily-run race plays to a jumper who can conserve energy, and with no genuine pace rival to threaten him early, he controls the fractions and wins on his own terms.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace set by Mongibello creates a target that a genuine hold-up horse tracks comfortably before asserting on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Daydream Nation (2W4P on similar going, won at 24f on soft) has the staying profile to come with a well-timed run off a slow tempo, and Feet On The Ground, despite lower-rated, has proven hold-up credentials and course-type experience. A truly moderate gallop can compress the field late and reward the horse who travels most easily without expending early energy.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Force Pace Up
scenarios.trigger: If Ndaawi, Captain Ryan Matt or Polepatrick refuse to be restrained and push Mongibello into a faster-than-ideal early gallop.
scenarios.body: If the redistributed prominent runners impose themselves and stretch the pace, Mongibello risks not finishing as strongly off 501 days, and a horse like Ocastle Des Mottes (Paul Townend, Mullins, OR 126, 2nd on similar going) with class and tactical versatility could benefit from a more truly-run race. Captain Ryan Matt's De Bromhead connection and strong sim-going record (2W3P) also becomes more relevant if the race is run at an honest clip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Chaos At Fences
scenarios.trigger: If the novice nature of this beginners' chase produces jumping errors, fallers or a messy race that turns into a test of jumping accuracy over stamina.
scenarios.body: A beginners' chase over 2m2f on yielding ground with 8 novices always carries fall/unseating risk, and any major jumping incident could shuffle the order entirely and reward the most reliable jumper still standing. Polepatrick (headgear, sound jumping form) and William Tell (headgear, familiar with the trip range) have the profile to survive a chaotic passage.

watchPoints.text: Watch Mongibello's jumping from the first fence — any early error on comeback from 501 days could unsettle his rhythm and fundamentally change the race shape, opening the door for Ocastle Des Mottes or Daydream Nation.

If Ndaawi or Captain Ryan Matt fail to settle in midfield and press Mongibello early, the pace could spike into an uncharacteristically strong gallop that shortens the race for hold-up horses like Daydream Nation and Feet On The Ground.

Ocastle Des Mottes showed a missed run marker ('?') in his history — confirm the horse has come through that run cleanly before weighting his chance too heavily, even with Townend and Mullins attached.

This is a beginners' chase and multiple runners carry headgear (William Tell, Feet On The Ground, Polepatrick, Ndaawi) — watch for jumping errors at the open ditches where novices most commonly make costly mistakes in a race of this nature.

The going report confirms Yielding for this race despite the card listing Good to Soft — horses with soft/yielding form (Mongibello, Daydream Nation, Polepatrick) hold a meaningful edge over those whose form base is exclusively on good ground like William Tell.

runners_data.name: Tell Us This
runners_data.note: Three wins from eight runs on good ground is an excellent profile, and Andrew McNamara's runner arrives just 25 days since its last outing in decent form; natural hold-up horse bumped into midfield by the field's bias — the 0.93 style-fit score means it should get reasonably close to its preferred position, but Conor Stone-Walsh will need to be sharp for room.

runners_data.name: Granville Street

runners_data.name: Justatan

runners_data.name: Oneforgonzo
runners_data.note: Sean Aherne's eight-year-old carries a promising profile — one win over 20f on good ground and placed form at the trip — and 30 days since its last run is a comfortable interval; Phillip Enright partners a genuine hold-up horse pushed into midfield, and its 0.93 style-fit score suggests it will compete for its natural rear position, making a run from off the pace plausible.

runners_data.name: Nolans Rocco
runners_data.note: Padraig Butler runner returning after 150 days — the longest absence in the field — which is a significant freshness flag in a Galway handicap chase; form that includes wins on heavy (1st) and yielding (2nd) gives it a going angle, but no sim-going evidence on good ground and the long layoff make Michael Kenneally's task harder.

runners_data.name: Smallcraftwarning
runners_data.note: Won just three days ago for John Patrick Ryan (2W/11, 14 days) and represents the sharpest fitness edge in the field, though the rapid turnaround is a genuine stamina-drain concern over 2m6½f; Daniel King's mount is a proven turf performer (15/15 on sim going, 1W7P) and the winning form is compelling — the key question is whether three days' recovery is enough to sustain a late effort.

races.paceDynamic: Brandt is the only confirmed front-runner in this field and, redistributed to the lead from a natural hold-up role, will set a measured, uncontested gallop over 2m6½f on yielding ground at Galway — a track that places a premium on jumping fluency and stamina in the closing stages. With Carl Millar (5) in the saddle and 90 days off the track, Brandt's ability to sustain that lead under minimal pressure makes this a single-pace, controlled affair rather than a searching test from the front. The overwhelming hold-up bias across this field — eleven runners, virtually all naturally drawn to race off the pace — means the closing stages will see a bunched cavalry charge, with those who travel widest or get first run at the second-last likely to dictate the finish. This race shape strongly favours genuine hold-up horses with proven stamina, clean jumping records, and the ability to quicken off a moderate gallop on yielding ground. The field carries far more prominent and hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear: Tell Us This, Granville Street, Juke Hill, Justatan, Oneforgonzo, That's About Right, Nolans Rocco and Smallcraftwarning are all natural hold-up horses shuffled into midfield positions they will compete for aggressively, meaning the pace scenario is genuinely congested; Brandt is most likely to secure the lead, with Tonaghneave Well and Tullybeg the most likely to settle closest to it among the rest.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Brandt Controls, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Brandt dictates a sustainable single-file gallop and the hold-up pack stalks before unleashing a wave finish from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Brandt's uncontested lead keeps the tempo honest but not truly searching, setting up a test of finishing stamina and jumping accuracy over the final two fences; horses with proven form at this trip on good-to-yielding ground and clean jumping records will be best placed to sweep past.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Congestion Causes Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pack of hold-up types fails to find gaps early in the straight and a midfield horse quickens first into the final fence.
scenarios.body: The scramble for position among the redistributed hold-up horses creates a wall of runners turning in, and any horse with a clear passage and an agile jump at the last earns a decisive advantage; this scenario rewards whoever gets first run from a covered position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Smallcraftwarning Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses approaching the last and the race is run at a crawl, setting up a flat-out sprint finish over the final two obstacles.
scenarios.body: Smallcraftwarning won three days ago and carries fatigue risk, but on yielding ground over this trip its form-string of a recent win and proven stamina could allow it to close fastest of all off a slow tempo; the key is whether it has recovered sufficiently to produce a genuine late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Brandt Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly moderate and Brandt finds racing in front — out of its natural hold-up role — to its advantage by conserving energy throughout.
scenarios.body: Racing well within itself from the front, Brandt could simply outstay rivals who fail to produce their kick from off the pace in the closing stages; its decent form on good-to-yielding ground (14/15 sim-going) gives it a genuine profile for this ground, even if the style-fit discount applies.

watchPoints.text: Smallcraftwarning ran and won just three days ago — Daniel King must be monitored closely for any signs of fatigue from the second-last fence, where its recent exertion could cost it the lead in the closing stages.

The mass of hold-up horses (Tell Us This, Granville Street, Juke Hill, Justatan, Oneforgonzo, That's About Right, Nolans Rocco, Smallcraftwarning) will create severe congestion turning for home — watch for scrimmaging and lost momentum at the final bend that could cause interference or falls.

Brandt's 90-day absence and 0/9 trainer form in the past 14 days for Cian Collins raises a fitness concern at the front — if Brandt weakens sharply after the second-last, the pace vacuum could trigger a bunched cavalry-charge finish with significant fall risk.
Nolans Rocco returns after 150 days off the track with no confirmed going evidence on today's ground — watch its jumping early to assess whether it is fit enough to last home at this trip.

Tell Us This (3W from 8 on good ground) and Tonaghneave Well (2W7P on sim going) both carry strong going profiles for today's conditions — watch how quickly each jockey moves to secure a clear run from the rear of the midfield pack entering the straight.
